subject: Operations
title: Kodak's Digital Blind Spot
description: A quick win: understand Kodak's Digital Blind Spot.

hook.text: Kodak invented the digital camera in 1975. Then buried it to protect film profits. By 2012, Kodak was bankrupt.

buildup.text: Kodak dominated photography for a century. Film, chemicals, and paper were a massively profitable operations machine.

discovery.text: Kodak's operations were optimized for film. Every factory, supply chain, and process assumed film would last forever.

twist.text: When digital cameras took over, Kodak's entire operations infrastructure became obsolete overnight.

climax.text: Kodak's failure wasn't ignorance—they invented digital. It was an operations strategy locked to the wrong product.

punchline.text: Optimizing for yesterday's product guarantees tomorrow's bankruptcy.

quiz.question: When did Kodak invent the digital camera?
